title: Characterization of children and adolescents with chronic pain and evaluation of their interdisciplinary multimodal pain therapy
summary:
Chronic pain in children and adolescents represents a significant burden for those affected as well as for their families. At the same time, it results in high socioeconomic costs. Given the increasing prevalence of chronic pain in young patients in Germany, the provision of healthcare in specialized pain centers for children and adolescents needs to be extended and optimized. This includes a comprehensive diagnosis through an interdisciplinary pain assessment and an interdisciplinary, multimodal pain therapy (IMPT). The Multidisciplinary Pain Center and Outpatient Clinic at the Campus City Center of the Department of Anaesthesiology of the LMU Hospital contributes to complete this health care requirement in cooperation with the Dr. von Hauner Children’s Hospital. The interdisciplinary pain assessment for children and adolescents has already been established and since the year 2025 an IMPT-program has been offered particularly for this age group.
In order to sustain a long-term scientific evaluation of this healthcare offer the research project presented here operates the analysis of routine patient data. These clinical routine data consist of psychometric patient questionnaires as diagnostic results documented by the physicians.
The first aim is to explore whether certain characteristics of children and adolescents with chronic pain and of their parents demand particular treatment approaches or their adaptation. In order to gain the highest possible insight into characteristics and behaviors of children and adolescents with chronic pain, a comparison with children and adolescents without chronic pain, but matched for age, gender and education status, will be conducted. For this purpose, children and adolescents will be pooled together with their parents in and around the city of Munich.
The second aim is to evaluate the effectiveness of the IMPT offered to children and adolescents by means of routine patient data that are collected before and at several time points after IMST.
conditions: Chronic pain disorder with somatic and psychological factors

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Clinical sample:
• Children and adolescents with chronic pain and their legal guardians
• Legal guardians must be of legal age
• Completion of an interdisciplinary pain assessment of the child/adolescent at the Multidisciplinary Pain Center, Campus City Center, Department for Anesthesiology, LMU University Hospital
•    Proficiency in the German language
•    Intellectual ability to answer a questionnaire
•    Written consent of the child/adolescent and both legal guardians
Comparison sample:
• Children and adolescents and their legal guardians
• Legal guardians must be of legal age
• Children must be between 11 and 17 years of age
• Children/adolescents must not suffer from chronic pain (persistent or recurring pain for at least three months) 
• No serious illness in the child/adolescent that severely impairs their life
• Proficiency in the German language
• Intellectual ability to answer a questionnaire
Exclusion criteria:
Clinical sample and comparison sample:
• Malignant disease of the child/adolescent
• Life-limiting disease of the child/adolescent
